# nomadpack Provider

Drives nomad-pack (https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/tools/nomad-pack) deployments as Terraform resources by wrapping the nomad-pack CLI's own plan/run/destroy lifecycle, so nomad-pack's meta tracking remains the single source of truth for what's deployed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    nomadpack = {
      source  = "byteford/nomadpack"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "nomadpack" {
  # All of these are optional and fall back to the same NOMAD_ADDR,
  # NOMAD_NAMESPACE, NOMAD_TOKEN, etc. environment variables nomad-pack
  # itself reads, so in most setups you don't need to set anything here.
  address    = "https://nomad.example.internal:4646"
  namespace  = "default"
  run_detach = false

  # Recommended: makes relative paths in `pack`/`var_files` resolve
  # against your Terraform root, instead of depending on whatever working
  # directory Terraform happens to launch the provider subprocess with.
  working_directory = path.root

  # If more than one machine (or user) runs Terraform, set this to the same
  # absolute path everywhere. nomad-pack records the path of a registry pack
  # in each job's `pack.path` meta, so without it, applying from a different
  # machine changes the meta and restarts the job. Linux/Unix only.
  cache_dir = "/var/cache/homelab"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `address` (String) Nomad server address. Falls back to the NOMAD_ADDR environment variable read by nomad-pack itself if unset.
- `binary_path` (String) Path to the nomad-pack binary. Defaults to "nomad-pack" resolved from PATH.
- `ca_cert` (String) Path to a PEM encoded CA cert to verify the Nomad server's TLS certificate.
- `cache_dir` (String) Absolute directory under which nomad-pack keeps its registry cache, set as XDG_CACHE_HOME for every nomad-pack call (the cache ends up in `<cache_dir>/nomad/packs`). nomad-pack records the path of the pack it deployed in each job's `pack.path` meta, and a meta change restarts the job, so use the same path on every machine that runs Terraform, otherwise applying from a different machine or user restarts jobs that use a registry pack. Only takes effect on Linux and other Unix systems; nomad-pack ignores XDG_CACHE_HOME on macOS and Windows. Left unset, nomad-pack uses its default (`~/.cache/nomad/packs`). Changing it starts with an empty cache.
- `client_cert` (String) Path to a PEM encoded client certificate for TLS authentication. Requires client_key.
- `client_key` (String, Sensitive) Path to the unencrypted PEM encoded private key matching client_cert.
- `namespace` (String) Nomad namespace. Falls back to NOMAD_NAMESPACE if unset.
- `region` (String) Nomad region. Falls back to NOMAD_REGION if unset.
- `run_detach` (Boolean) Pass -detach to nomad-pack run/destroy so Terraform doesn't block waiting for deployments/evaluations to finish healing. Defaults to false.
- `tls_server_name` (String) SNI host to use when connecting via TLS.
- `tls_skip_verify` (Boolean) Skip TLS certificate verification. Not recommended.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) Nomad ACL token. Falls back to NOMAD_TOKEN if unset.
- `working_directory` (String) Working directory for every nomad-pack subprocess invocation. Left unset, the subprocess inherits the provider process's own working directory — which Terraform does not guarantee matches the directory you actually run `terraform apply` from, since it launches provider plugin binaries as separate subprocesses. Relative paths in a resource's `pack` or `var_files` that look correct can still fail to resolve as a result. Set this to `path.root` to remove that ambiguity: `working_directory = path.root`.
